title: Lesson Plan — Lines and Angles (Class 6 CBSE)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Distinguish point, line, line segment and ray.
Identify the vertex and arms of an angle and name angles correctly.
Use a protractor to measure and draw angles.
Classify angles by type (acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex).
Identify parallel, intersecting and perpendicular lines.
Apply the linear-pair and vertically-opposite-angles rules at an intersection.
prerequisites: Familiarity with basic shapes from earlier grades.
Comfort with the Cartesian-style notion of position.
materials: One protractor per pair of students
Photocopies with blank angles to measure
Cards labelled with angle measures (e.g. 25°, 90°, 135°, 200°) for a 'classify the angle' card sort

activities.description: Hook with a 'spot the angles' challenge. Project a photo of a classroom or a building. Ask students to point out as many angles as they can in 60 seconds. Make a quick tally on the board.
teacher_actions: Project the image; start a 60-second timer.
Take a tally of angle types spotted.
student_actions: Spot angles and call them out.

activities.description: Pair card sort. Distribute angle-measure cards (10°, 45°, 90°, 100°, 135°, 180°, 200°, 270°). Pairs sort into bins labelled acute / right / obtuse / straight / reflex.
teacher_actions: Distribute card sets and bin labels.

activities.description: Direct instruction in four blocks: (i) point, line, segment, ray with vocabulary; (ii) angles — vertex/arms/naming; (iii) measuring with a protractor (live demo with a 60° angle); (iv) types of angles by measure; (v) parallel/intersecting/perpendicular and the two key rules at intersections.
teacher_actions: Define each basic object with a sketch.
Demonstrate the four-step protractor procedure live.
Sketch the five angle types side-by-side.
Draw two crossing lines; label one angle; derive the other three using the rules.
student_actions: Add the protractor steps to a 'rules box'.

activities.description: Hands-on activity. Each pair gets a worksheet with 5 angles to measure with a protractor and 3 angles to draw. Then they verify partner's measurements.
teacher_actions: Circulate; correct protractor placement / scale errors.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Measure each angle to the nearest degree.
Draw three new angles of given measures.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 5 questions — 2 classification, 1 angle naming, 2 intersection rules.
Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Find three angles in your home or street, sketch them, and classify each.' Preview Chapter 3 (Number Play).
teacher_actions: Bridge to Chapter 3 with a quick number-pattern teaser.

homework: Complete the rest of the Worksheet — Lines and Angles handout.
Find three angles in your home or street; sketch each and classify it (acute/right/obtuse/straight/reflex).
Use a protractor to draw angles of 35°, 100°, and 150°.
assessment_ideas: Mark the LONG_ANSWER on linear-pair algebra using the auto-grade rubric.
Peer-grading on the 'angles in your home' homework using a two-criterion rubric (sketch + correct classification).
references: NCERT Class 6 Mathematics — Ganita Prakash, Chapter 2: Lines and Angles.
